deck.caption:
The Enforcement Directorate has frozen Rs 200 crore across 29 locations in a major 'pump and dump' investigation. This isn't just a headline; it's a warning about how your money can get trapped when you chase sudden stock spikes. 

In this carousel, we break down:
• How 'pump and dump' schemes artificially inflate prices.
• Why your capital gets locked during regulatory raids.
• How to spot the difference between real growth and market manipulation.

Save this post to keep your investment strategy grounded. 

Do you check a company's business performance before buying, or do you rely on price trends? 

#MarketSafety #InvestingTips #StockMarketIndia #FinancialAwareness #PumpAndDump

slides.title: Raids across 29 premises and Rs 200 crore frozen: The hidden cost of 'Pump and Dump' scams.
slides.body: When a stock price jumps for no reason, you might be funding someone else's exit. Here is what happens when the regulators step in.

slides.title: What is a 'Pump and Dump'?
slides.content: It is a scheme where manipulators artificially inflate ('pump') the price of a stock through false information or fake trading volume. Once the price is high, they sell ('dump') their shares to unsuspecting investors, causing the price to crash.
slides.card_text: card_text It is a scheme where manipulators artificially inflate ('pump') the price of a stock through false information or fake trading volume. Once the price is high, they sell ('dump') their shares to unsuspecting investors, causing the price to crash.

slides.title: The Scale of the Investigation
slides.content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) recently conducted raids across 29 premises in Maharashtra and Gujarat, leading to the freezing of Rs 200 crore in trading accounts linked to these activities.
slides.card_text: stat_data The Enforcement Directorate (ED) recently conducted raids across 29 premises in Maharashtra and Gujarat, leading to the freezing of Rs 200 crore in trading accounts linked to these activities.

slides.title: Why do accounts get frozen?
slides.content: When regulators suspect market manipulation, they freeze accounts to prevent the movement of funds while they investigate. If your money is in an account under investigation, you may lose access to your own capital for an indefinite period.
slides.card_text: card_text When regulators suspect market manipulation, they freeze accounts to prevent the movement of funds while they investigate. If your money is in an account under investigation, you may lose access to your own capital for an indefinite period.

slides.title: Myth vs. Reality
slides.content: Myth: A rapidly rising stock price means the company is doing great. Reality: A sudden, unexplained spike in price and volume is often a red flag for artificial manipulation rather than genuine business growth.
slides.card_text: comparison_data Myth: A rapidly rising stock price means the company is doing great. Reality: A sudden, unexplained spike in price and volume is often a red flag for artificial manipulation rather than genuine business growth.

slides.title: How to Protect Your Capital
slides.content: 1. Ignore 'hot tips' on social media. 2. Check the company's official financial reports. 3. Look for consistent business performance. 4. Avoid buying stocks just because they are hitting new highs daily.
slides.card_text: flowchart_data 1. Ignore 'hot tips' on social media. 2. Check the company's official financial reports. 3. Look for consistent business performance. 4. Avoid buying stocks just because they are hitting new highs daily.

slides.title: Quick Safety Checklist
slides.content: Does the company have a clear business model? [Pass/Fail] | Is the price rise backed by public financial results? [Pass/Fail] | Are you buying based on a 'tip'? [Pass/Fail]
slides.card_text: checklist_data Does the company have a clear business model? [Pass/Fail] | Is the price rise backed by public financial results? [Pass/Fail] | Are you buying based on a 'tip'? [Pass/Fail]

slides.title: Invest in Facts, Not Trends
slides.body: Always verify a company's fundamental health before investing. If a stock's movement seems too good to be true, it usually is. Save this post to remind yourself to look deeper before you trade.
slides.cta_detail: Save this post to your 'Investment Safety' folder.
